perspective: Adversarial Finance verification of distribution, fringe, FTE, pay-period, Oracle-deadline, and configuration-year claims

findings.claim: Multiple-account distributions must be calculated per pay period and total 100%; the cited example is 90% ENG plus 10% grant.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:167-183 — Daisy says the distribution must add to 100% during the stipend pay period and gives 90% ENG + 10% grant.
daisy_finance_stage.md:23-25 — summary states per-pay-period distributions must total 100%.
findings.risk: The arithmetic example is internally valid (90 + 10 = 100), but no worked grad-student example or validation rule for rounding, overlapping periods, zero/negative percentages, or amount-vs-percent entry is provided.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-pay-period validation with exact 100% total, bounded nonnegative percentages, explicit rounding policy, and period-overlap checks; test with a grad-student case separately.

findings.claim: Fringe is lookup-driven and changes by configuration year; 35.5% faculty and 42% administrative are cited values.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:412-426 — Daisy identifies the 2627 fringe rate example as 35.5% for faculty and changes it to 42% for administrative.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:426-450 — Daisy requests annual changeability; Ian proposes editable/importable configuration.
daisy_finance_stage.md:23-26 — summary records the rates as examples and says the lookup changes yearly.
findings.risk: These rates are explicitly a faculty/administrative example, not a verified graduate-student fringe policy. Applying them globally could miscost student appointments.
findings.recommendation: Key rates by effective configuration year, worker/job category, and possibly appointment type; require an effective date and prevent silent retroactive recalculation. Obtain authoritative grad-student fringe rates before implementation.

findings.claim: FTE is derived from hours; 10 hours maps to 0.25 FTE and 20 hours maps to 0.50 FTE.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:983-985 — Daisy states the HR FTE chart maps 10 hours to 0.25 and 20 hours to 0.5 and says the formula is in the chart.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1007-1015 — Daisy says the worksheet has hours but no formula and asks for automatic FTE calculation.
findings.risk: The examples imply hours/40, but the transcript does not explicitly establish the denominator, rounding, maximum hours, or whether FTE is weekly, appointment-period, or job-code-specific. Do not elevate the inferred formula to policy.
findings.recommendation: Use the authoritative HR FTE chart as the source; capture denominator, valid range, precision, and job-category exceptions. Label hours/40 as an inference until the chart is inspected.

findings.claim: Pay periods and check dates are required inputs, and the calendar is updated annually.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:454-462 — Daisy says she consults the HR/payroll tab for pay periods and check dates and that it is updated every year.
daisy_finance_stage.md:23-26 — summary places the calendar in distribution and Oracle costing.
findings.risk: No actual pay-period dates, check dates, calendar version, fiscal-year boundary, or handling for appointments spanning periods is present; calculations cannot be independently recomputed from the transcript.
findings.recommendation: Require a versioned effective-dated payroll calendar with exact period start/end and check dates; validate that every costing/distribution period resolves to one calendar row.

findings.claim: Costing must be entered in Oracle by a pay-period deadline, and the deadline matters for RSA checks.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:470-482 — Daisy says RSA checks require costing changes in Oracle by a stated but unspecified time.
daisy_finance_stage.md:26-27 — summary says enter costing by the pay-period deadline.
findings.risk: The transcript does not state the deadline date/time, timezone, owner, cutoff rule, exception path, or whether the cutoff is period-specific. A system cannot safely enforce a deadline from this evidence alone.
findings.recommendation: Obtain the authoritative deadline schedule and ownership; model deadlines as effective-dated calendar data rather than a single hard-coded cutoff.

findings.claim: At least fringe rates and pay-period/check-date calendars change by year and must be configurable.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:426-450 — annual fringe-rate change and editable/importable configuration are explicitly discussed.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:454-468 — pay periods/check dates are updated every year and should be available in the system.
findings.risk: The evidence does not define whether configuration is academic year, fiscal year, calendar year, or payroll year, nor effective-date precedence when a record crosses years.
findings.recommendation: Store configuration with explicit year label plus effective start/end dates, audit history, importer validation, and a rule for cross-year appointments.

findings.claim: The costing examples prove the Finance rules for graduate-student appointments.
evidence: daisy_finance_stage.md:8-11 — explicitly says Daisy supports faculty/staff, Mayra supports grad students, and Daisy's worked examples were faculty, not students.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:83-101 — Michelle King stipend example is presented as a faculty/department account distribution.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:167-183 — Dr. Casanova stipend and 90/10 distribution example.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:412-426 — fringe examples are faculty and administrative categories.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:983-1015 — FTE examples are described as HR/Laura calculations, but no student-specific costing example is worked.
findings.risk: A finance implementation based only on these examples may apply faculty/staff stipend, fringe, or distribution assumptions to graduate students without evidence.
findings.recommendation: Keep faculty/staff examples labeled as such; obtain and verify at least one graduate-student appointment covering salary, FTE, fringe applicability, chartfield, split distribution, pay period, and Oracle cutoff.

missing_or_ambiguous: Exact pay-period start/end dates and check dates for the relevant configuration year.
Exact Oracle costing deadline(s), timezone, owner, and late-entry handling.
Authoritative graduate-student fringe policy/rates and whether fringe applies to each student appointment type.
Authoritative FTE formula denominator, precision, valid range, and exceptions by job code/category.
Rounding and validation rules for percentage distributions and salary/fringe amounts.
Effective-date/year semantics for appointments spanning configuration-year changes.
Whether the 90/10 distribution and 35.5%/42% fringe values are illustrative only or current policy values.
Exact post-entry worksheet status: transcript says 'page'; derived artifact says probably 'paid', so status is unresolved.
